value_policy.rationale: C1 is an architecture preparation hypothesis. Preserve resource and semantic behavior; a speed claim needs at least 5% improvement above noise, and an equivalence claim requires uncertainty within 3%. Shared code alone is not performance progress.

selected_idea.bottleneck: XSwap depends on ZSwap global policy and lifetime because the compression/storage mechanism is embedded in that frontend.
selected_idea.mechanism: Extract crypto-acomp CPU contexts and zsmalloc object store into page_compress; adapt ZSwap without moving indexes, charges, admission or LRU ownership.
selected_idea.expected_benefit: Reusable compressed-object mechanism with preserved existing frontend behavior; establishes preparation for later independent XSwap, not a presumed speedup.
selected_idea.simpler_alternative: Retain the integrated ZSwap implementation, or reuse crypto-acomp alone and duplicate pool/context cleanup in a new frontend.
selected_idea.falsifier: Reject on ownership/charge drift, failed real compressed-path/lifecycle coverage, new metadata or context footprint, or calibrated swap-in guard regression.
required_evidence: Exact-tree independent API, ownership, lock and failure review
Eight counted configuration-bound correctness boots and disabled build coverage
Real nonzero compressed residency, demand decode and no lower backing for compressed timing
Fresh same-protocol probe and fast calibration with all guards
selected_idea.no_upstream_reason: The exact original XSwap/ZSwap implementation is the common control. Reusing crypto-acomp directly would retain duplicated pool/context cleanup; replacing it with zram zcomp changes allocator and hotplug behavior. No separate compatible page/object-library arm was identified in the pinned source audit.
selected_idea.selection_reason: Test the minimum shared mechanism boundary before independent frontend and migration state changes.

state.reason: Keep frontend entry layout, pool IDs, policy and logical indexes; add no object wrapper.

lifetime.reason: Frontend lifetime pins remain; library explicitly owns context and object-pool destruction.

locking.reason: Retain per-CPU context mutex and synchronous crypto completion; frontend locks remain.

error_paths.reason: Move allocation and crypto cleanup into common mechanism while preserving categories and rollback.

configuration.reason: Add hidden library and focused KUnit configuration; validate disabled clients and legacy ZSwap.

test_burden.reason: Require pool/context errors, NUMA/hotplug, memcg, large-folio, KASAN/lockdep/KCSAN coverage.

interfaces.reason: A small handle/length API separates compression mechanism from frontend ownership.

memory_cost.reason: Preserve compact entry metadata, zsmalloc handles and existing per-CPU workspace sizes.
